title: Three woods loop
ring: Nature XL · Couthofbos · Canadabos · De Lovie · {{KM}} km ·
sub: North to the woods and the castle park, home along Provenseweg.
desc: An {{KM}} km loop from Kleine Dasdreef over the old railway to Couthofbos, Canadabos and De Lovie, Poperinge.

waypoints.name: Home
waypoints.title: Out of the door
waypoints.note: Down the gravel lane to Kleine Dasdreef, then left and west on Helleketelweg; at the Karel Grimminckweg junction take Duivinnestraat north.
waypoints.accent: Clockwise. The woods come between kilometre six and eleven.

waypoints.name: Old railway
waypoints.label: Old railway
waypoints.title: Left onto the old railway bed
waypoints.note: The Poperinge to Hazebrouck line, now a car-free path. West to Sint-Jan-ter-Biezen.

waypoints.name: Sint-Jan-ter-Biezen
waypoints.label: Sint-Jan-ter-Biezen
waypoints.title: Sint-Jan-ter-Biezen
waypoints.note: Chapel hamlet. Leave the railway and head north: the lane climbs gently past the hop farms towards Blokstraat and Gravendreef.

waypoints.name: Gravendreef
waypoints.label: Gravendreef
waypoints.title: Right into Gravendreef
waypoints.note: The dreef runs straight at the wood. Limited parking at the end; from here it is walkers only.

waypoints.name: Couthofbos
waypoints.label: Couthofbos
waypoints.title: Couthofbos
waypoints.note: Sessile oaks, some of them very old; the signs say the oldest tree of Poperinge stands here. Take the path north-east through the wood.
waypoints.accent: Quiet wood. You may have it to yourself.

waypoints.name: Couthofbos north
waypoints.title: Out at the north side
waypoints.note: Leave the wood towards Couthoflaan, cross it with care (it is the busiest road of the day) and follow the lane north towards Canadabos.

waypoints.name: Canadabos
waypoints.label: Canadabos
waypoints.title: Canadabos
waypoints.note: A wood with a strange history: under the leaves lies a concrete launch pad for V1 flying bombs from 1944. Information board at the entrance.

waypoints.name: De Lovie
waypoints.label: De Lovie
waypoints.title: De Lovie
waypoints.note: The castle of De Lovie, 19th century, with its park and ponds, today a care home. The lane skirts the park; the gardens are open on weekdays.

waypoints.name: Krombeekseweg
waypoints.title: South on Provenseweg
waypoints.note: From the castle gate head south-east, then south along Provenseweg, a long straight lane towards Poperinge.

waypoints.name: Provenseweg
waypoints.label: Provenseweg
waypoints.title: Long straight south
waypoints.note: Hop fields and farms. The town appears ahead; stay on the lane until the ring road.

waypoints.name: Ring road
waypoints.title: Cross the ring road
waypoints.note: A short stretch beside the ring, then Provenseweg continues south-west out of town. Then Provenstraat, Helleketelweg and the dreef home.

goodtoknow: A long one on quiet lanes, with three woods and the old railway as the unpaved parts. Two roads to respect: Couthoflaan north of Couthofbos and the ring road at Poperinge; both have a crossing within a few metres of the line.
Nothing to eat or drink on the way except what you carry; the one café is De Lovie's on weekdays. Plan a good half day.
more: Couthofbos and the Couthof estate are the oldest woodland around Poperinge. Canadabos is named after the Canadian troops of 1944 and still hides a V1 launch base in the undergrowth. De Lovie, between them, is a neo-Gothic castle of the 1850s in a landscaped park with ponds, now a care institution that opens its gardens to visitors.
The way out follows the old railway to Sint-Jan-ter-Biezen; the way back follows Provenseweg, which was the medieval road from Poperinge to Proven.
tlcue: Clockwise. Distances are from the front door.
